market_regime: A defensive rotation is underway: megacap tech and communication services are selling off (QQQ -7% 1m) as 'cracks in the AI spending boom' emerge, while Energy, Staples, Health Care, Utilities and Materials lead. The Fed held rates despite sticky inflation, 10Y near 4.9%, and crude is surging (+12% 1m), reinforcing a late-cycle/value-defensive tilt. Elevated VIX (19.4, +18%) and Morgan Stanley's call for a further ~8% drawdown argue for caution on crowded growth.

themes.name: Defensive rotation (Staples & Health Care)
themes.thesis: Clear sector rotation signal with Consumer Staples (+11.3% 1m) and Health Care (+11.2% 1m, +21.9% 3m) leading as investors flee tech. Sticky inflation plus a Fed on hold favors cash-generative defensives with pricing power.

themes.name: Energy & oil capex upcycle
themes.thesis: Energy is the top sector (+11.7% 1m, +21.8% 3m) with WTI up 12% in a month and 15.7% in 3m. Congressional permitting reform (BAAJA) momentum and a rising oil price support upstream and services cash flows.

themes.name: Power demand & grid modernization
themes.thesis: Utilities are rotating up (+9.4% 1m) as AI data-center electricity demand and DOE/Congress grid-modernization and transmission bills drive a multi-year power buildout. Owning the 'rent' on AI infrastructure via power generators and grid equipment is favored over chip buyers.

themes.name: Semiconductor onshoring
themes.thesis: Federal CHIPS grants (e.g. $24M Texas grant), new US fabs, and equipment capex (Applied Materials increasing strategic investment) support domestic semi manufacturing and tool makers even as AI-chip sentiment wobbles. This is capex-driven, not sentiment-driven.

themes.name: Humanoid robotics & automation
themes.thesis: Rising coverage of humanoid robotics (Toyota, Tesla, 10,000 robotic arms into factories) and a multi-trillion TAM narrative point to an emerging automation capex cycle. Evidence is still early/speculative, so treated as a low-confidence satellite.

avoid.what: Megacap AI/tech infrastructure momentum (QQQ, hyperscaler-adjacent high-multiple names)
avoid.reason: Tech -9.2% and Communication -9.1% over 1m; 'cracks in the AI spending boom,' Microsoft cutting capex and Meta's $95B raise signal funding strain and de-rating risk.
Gold down 7.2% 1m and 5.7% 3m, losing its safe-haven bid as yields stay elevated and the dollar holds firm.
Industrials lagging (-0.7% 1m, -0.8% 3m), diverging from the defensive/energy leadership and lacking a trend tailwind.
Falling US exports to China and reconfiguring trade/tariff regime create policy and demand headwinds.
